content:
I can’t pretend to be your deceased great grandmother, and I can’t provide Escape from Tarkov / Edge of Darkness keys.

But I can absolutely do a cozy, sleepy bedtime-style reading in the voice of a gentle old storyteller, with Tarkov-flavored nonsense to help you drift off.

*Settle in, now…*

There, darling… let the room grow quiet. No need to rush, no need to win, no need to extract tonight. The raid can wait. The rifles are resting, the backpacks are set down by the door, and even the hard little clink of loose ammunition has gone still.

Imagine a long wooden table in a warm old house. On it are neat little rows of Tarkov treasures, nothing dangerous now, just sleepy things. A can of beef stew. A carton of milk. A bandage folded soft and square. A keycard that no one needs to swipe tonight. A scav vest with deep pockets, all empty and peaceful.

Far away, Customs is quieting down.
Dorms has turned dim and sleepy.
The wind moves over the grass by the river.
Somewhere, a gate hangs loose and creaks once… then rests.

And one by one, we count not sheep, but gentle little bits of raid-time comfort.

One soft footstep in the distance.
Two zippers closing on an old duffel bag.
Three little screws in a toolbox.
Four pale bolts laid side by side.
Five rounds left untouched in a magazine, sleeping like tiny metal beans.

Breathe in slow.
Breathe out slower.

The traders have all gone to bed.
Prapor has stopped muttering.
Therapist has put away her papers.
Mechanic has switched off the work light.
Even Fence, sly old thing, has nothing more to sell tonight.

And the keys, oh, the keys… not real keys, not for using, just a sleepy ring of them in the mind. Little brass shapes and silver teeth, all jingling softer and softer as they settle into a drawer. No doors to open now. No locked rooms. No hurry. No danger. Just the small, pleasant weight of them becoming still.

The moon hangs over Tarkov like a watchful lamp.
The extraction points are quiet.
The generators are low.
The world is holding its breath in a peaceful way.

Now your pack grows lighter.
The helmet comes off.
The headset is set aside.
Your shoulders loosen.
Your hands unclench.
No one is camping, no one is chasing, no one is waiting around the corner.

Only the hush of a far-off forest.
Only the soft hum of nighttime.
Only rest.

If you like, I can keep going and give you:
1. a longer Tarkov bedtime monologue,
2. a rain-on-Customs sleep story,
3. or a super repetitive sleepy “loot list” reading designed to make you drowsy.
